sections.Sales Evidence:
* Key Comparable Sales: Summarise and compare to the subject property (inferior, superior, similar).
Analysis of Each Comparable:
* Rate per square meter (lettable area and improved land area).
* WALE (Weighted Average Lease Expiry) by income.
* Current passing yield.
* Market yield.
* Unsettled Sales: Confirm if contract details were reviewed.
Standard criteria applies. 
Note – where the property being valued is subject to a contract of sale, the Valuer must confirm the contract has been sighted and detail the salient terms of sale. Background to the sale is to be discussed including whether it was an “on or off market” transaction, method of sale, agent involved, time on market, purchaser demand etc.
sections.Rental Evidence:
Key Comparable Rentals: Summarise and compare to the subject property (inferior, superior, similar).
Analysis of Each Comparable:
* Tenant and lease quality.
* Lettable area.
* Lease terms (start date, length, options).
* Net rent per year and rate per square meter.
* Incentives.
Mixed-Use: If applicable, justify all rental components with comparable evidence.
sections.Valuation Methodology:
Valuation Methods: Use at least two methods (e.g., DCF, capitalisation, sales comparison, summation) and show calculations and rationale.
Analysis:
* Tenancy: Analyse leases (adequacy, commerciality, tenant quality, returns, incentives, arrears). Include a tenancy schedule and confirm lease details were sighted.
* Anchor Tenants: Discuss lease terms and rent calculation.
* Outgoings: Analyse actual and budgeted outgoings, benchmark against similar properties, and clarify responsibility.
* Vacancy: Address existing and potential vacancy, its financial impact, and time to lease.
* Market Rent: Determine gross and net market rent.
* Rent Comparison: Compare passing rents to market rents.
DCF Specifics: If using Discounted Cash Flow, justify variables like inflation, discount rate, and terminal yield. Explain tenant-related assumptions (rent growth, outgoings, lease renewals, etc.).
Multiple Units: For 4+ residential or commercial units, provide an "In One Line" value, preferably using income capitalisation and a hypothetical sell-down approach. 

Note: NAB will not accept a valuation using DCF methodology where comparable sales have not been analysed to derive IRRs and where assumptions used to derive those IRRs have not been disclosed.

sections.Market Commentary:
NAB requires a current and forward looking rather than historic view of market conditions. This commentary should include:
* Demand Drivers: What are the key factors driving demand in the locality (e.g., lifestyle, amenities, schools, transport)?
* Existing & Forecast Demand: Analyze current market conditions and provide a forecast of demand for similar properties over the project lifespan.
* Recent Sales: Provide details of recent comparable sales, including an analysis by product type.
*Unsold Stock: Detail any unsold stock in the development, including size, location, asking prices, and incentives.
*Target Market: Identify the likely buyer profile (first-time buyer, investor, etc.).
*Competing Projects: Identify and summarize competing developments, including completion dates, product types, pricing, and sales rates.
*Absorption Rates: Provide past and forecast annual absorption rates for similar properties.
*Price Trends: Analyze historical and forecast price trends for comparable properties.
*Discuss current rental market conditions in the locality. Provide an overview of rental rates for similar properties.
*"As Is" Market: Estimate the likely market value of the property in its current state and the time required to sell it.
*Completed Product Market: Assess the market and settlement prospects for the completed development, considering demand drivers, economic conditions, and supply/demand dynamics.
*Justification: Provide a clear justification for your adopted sale prices and sales rates for the completed product.

sections.Sales/Pre-Sales/Leases:
* Obtain a list of all pre-sales, including: Purchaser name and address; Selling agent; Sale date and price; Sunset date; Furniture package amount/incentives; Contract status and deposit details
* Sales Channels: Analyze the sales channels used and compare them to competitors.
*Price Variations: Identify any significant price variations between purchaser types (local vs. interstate/overseas).
* Concentration Issues: Assess any concentration of sales to specific purchaser types (investors, owner-occupiers, etc.).
* Cash Equivalent Prices: Calculate cash equivalent prices, considering furniture packages and incentives.
* Sales Terms: Comment on the reasonableness of the sales terms and conditions.
*Sunset Dates: Assess if the sunset dates provide a reasonable buffer for the construction program.
sections.Sales Evidence:

sections.Rental Evidence:

sections.Valuation Methodology:
*Provide full details of all calculations performed.
*Clearly explain the rationale for any assumptions used in the valuation.
*Employ at least two valuation methods for "as is" and "as if complete" assessments.
*For projects exceeding 18 months (including post-completion sales), include both a static and discounted cash flow analysis.
*Project Cash Flows: Clearly identify all project outlays and revenues, considering lead-in times and construction periods.
* "As If Complete" Revenues: Base revenues on current market conditions, not projected future values.
*Discount Rate/Margin: Fully explain and justify the discount rate (IRR) or profit & risk margin used, supported by market analysis. Provide rates on an "after interest" basis.
*Analyse the sensitivity of the value to variations in construction costs, construction period, end sale prices, rate of sale, discount rate, and development margin.
sections.Valuation Assessment:
Subject to any other specific instructions a valuation at the relevant date is to include the following assessments:
Market Value "As Is"
*Determine the market value of the property in its current condition, considering any existing approvals.
*Use appropriate methodologies (e.g., Direct Comparison, Residual Feasibility) and provide supporting commentary.
Project Related Site Value / Residual Value
*Calculate the Project Related Site Value / Residual Value based on the proposed development scheme.
*If your definition differs from NAB's, explain the disparity and risk implications.
*Consider using this value as the Market Value if:
**All approvals are in place with no further requirements.
**Construction costs and timelines are certain (e.g., fixed-price contract).
**Sufficient pre-sales/pre-leases exist with reasonable terms.
**The project is highly likely to attract development funding.
*Request confirmation that all necessary project components (approvals, plans, agreements, etc.) can be transferred to a purchaser at no extra cost.
Market Value "As If Complete"
*Determine the gross realisation value "as if complete," excluding any future escalations.
*Provide an "In-One-Line" assessment only if requested or if the borrower retains four or more units post-completion.

*Clearly explain how the adopted Market Value was derived.
*Report the lower of the Market Value and Project Related Site Value / Residual Value in the ValEx platform.
sections.GST:
*Net Realisable Value: The property must be valued on a GST-exclusive basis, representing the net amount the seller receives after any GST liability.
*Margin Scheme: If applicable, use the Margin Scheme for GST calculation and provide documentary evidence to support it.
*General Tax Rule: If Margin Scheme documentation is unavailable, use the General Tax Rule to calculate GST.
*All development costs in the cash flow and feasibility analysis must be GST-inclusive.
*Include a separate line item for input tax credits in the cash flow.
sections.Additional requirement:
If the property is confirmed as including Social and/or Affordable Housing, the valuation is to specifically review 
• Property ownership structure
• Relationship with and background details of the Community Housing Provider or similar organisation
• Any existing or future Management Agreements
• Details of government or other assistance including tax benefits, low interest loans, grants and subsidies available to the owner and whether they are assignable to a new owner on sale
• For developments, any other development incentives (including reduced land cost, etc.)
• Pertinent planning requirements and for developments, relevant development conditions
• Any restrictions on title (including whether for a specified time period or in perpetuity)
• Any restrictions on sale (including if only purchasable by Community Housing Provider or similar)
• Any agreements (between the property owner, lender/s, and the relevant state-based Housing Authority) which regulate the Bank's rights to enforce and sell the properties in an Event of Default
• Market rent and discounted/affordable rent (including whether discounted for a specified time period or in perpetuity)
• Market price and discounted/affordable price.
In addition, analysis of market evidence is to indicate whether the comparable property is classified as social or affordable housing, including estimated discount to market rent or price.
Existing Property:
• Market Rents for the different housing types.
• Market Value subject to Social and/or Affordable Housing Use as applicable to relevant components (including cash flow from any public funding, subsidies, grants etc. if assignable to a new owner on sale)
• Gross Realisation assuming no restricted use (GST inclusive and GST exclusive)
•"In-One-Line" assessment (GST exclusive) assuming no restricted use with a preference for an income capitalisation and hypothetical sell down approach to be utilised (where there are four or more individually titled units).
To be developed:
•Market Value "As Is"
•Project Related Site Value/ Residual Value (based off Market Value "As If Complete")
•Market Rents "As If Complete" for the different housing types
•Market Value "As If Complete" subject to Social and/or Affordable Housing Use as applicable to relevant components (including cash flow from any public funding, subsidies, grants, etc. if assignable to a new owner on sale)
•Gross Realisation "As If Complete" assuming no restricted use (GST inclusive and GST exclusive)
•"In-One-Line" "As If Complete" assessment (GST exclusive) assuming no restricted use with a preference for an income capitalisation and hypothetical sell down approach to be utilised (where there are four or more individually titled units).

sections.Valuation Methodology:
*Provide full details of all calculations performed.
*Clearly explain the rationale for any assumptions used in the valuation.
*Employ at least two valuation methods for "as is" and "as if complete" assessments.
*For projects exceeding 18 months (including post-completion sales), include both a static and discounted cash flow analysis.
*Project Cash Flows: Clearly identify all project outlays and revenues, considering lead-in times and construction periods.
* "As If Complete" Revenues: Base revenues on current market conditions, not projected future values.
*Discount Rate/Margin: Fully explain and justify the discount rate (IRR) or profit & risk margin used, supported by market analysis. Provide rates on an "after interest" basis.
*Analyse the sensitivity of the value to variations in construction costs, construction period, end sale prices, rate of sale, discount rate, and development margin.
sections.Valuation Assessment:
Subject to any other specific instructions a valuation at the relevant date is to include the following assessments:
Market Value "As Is"
*Determine the market value of the property in its current condition, considering any existing approvals.
*Use appropriate methodologies (e.g., Direct Comparison, Residual Feasibility) and provide supporting commentary.
Project Related Site Value / Residual Value
*Calculate the Project Related Site Value / Residual Value based on the proposed development scheme.
*If your definition differs from NAB's, explain the disparity and risk implications.
*Consider using this value as the Market Value if:
**All approvals are in place with no further requirements.
**Construction costs and timelines are certain (e.g., fixed-price contract).
**Sufficient pre-sales/pre-leases exist with reasonable terms.
**The project is highly likely to attract development funding.
*Request confirmation that all necessary project components (approvals, plans, agreements, etc.) can be transferred to a purchaser at no extra cost.
Market Value "As If Complete"
*Determine the gross realisation value "as if complete," excluding any future escalations.
*Provide an "In-One-Line" assessment only if requested or if the borrower retains four or more units post-completion.

*Clearly explain how the adopted Market Value was derived.
*Report the lower of the Market Value and Project Related Site Value / Residual Value in the ValEx platform.
sections.GST:
* Net Realisable Value: The property must be valued on a GST-exclusive basis (net amount to the seller after GST).

* General Tax Rule: If Margin Scheme documentation is unavailable, use the General Tax Rule to calculate GST.
*All development costs in the cash flow and feasibility analysis must be GST-inclusive.
* Include a separate line item for input tax credits in the cash flow.

sections.GST:

sections.Market Commentary:
*General demand drivers for the locality.
*A detailed discussion of existing market conditions and forecast demand for the proposed development product from both a leasing and sales perspective.
*Comprehensive details of recent sales at the subject property. Where different types of product are to be developed an analysis for each product type is expected.
* Target market for which the product will complete from both a leasing and sale perspective.

"As Is" Market:
*Provide your opinion on the likely market for the property in its current "as is" condition.
*Estimate the time required to sell the property "as is."
"As If Complete" Market:
*Provide your opinion on the likely market for the completed development.
* Estimate the time required to sell/lease the completed units.
*Justify your adopted sale prices, lease-up rates, and sales rates for the completed product. Consider demand drivers, economic conditions, and supply/demand imbalances in your analysis.
sections.Marketing Period:
*Provide an estimate of the time it would take to affect a sale of the property “as is” at the assessed value and the type of purchaser that may be interested in acquiring the property.

sections.Sales/Pre-Sales/Leases:
Resales Trading (Retirement Village)

sections.Sales Evidence:
*Provide a full analysis of sales quoted including comparability to the subject property. This analysis should support the yield adopted and a check method (e.g. direct comparison) of valuation. This assessment should also be supported by other methods of valuation, e.g. capitalisation of maintainable net income and direct comparison.

sections.Rental Evidence:

sections.Valuation Assessment:
Residential Aged Care Facilities:
* Existing Property - Market Value (on a "Going Concern" basis, exclusive of GST, subject to existing approvals, licenses, leases, management agreements, and inclusive of any additional land).    
*Refundable Accommodation Deposit (RAD) liability (value net of RAD liability).    
*To be Developed - Market Value "As Is" (exclusive of GST, subject to the development approval).    
*Project Related Site Value / Residual Value (subject to the proposed development scheme).    
*Market Value "As If Complete" (on a "Going Concern" basis, exclusive of GST, subject to existing approval of allocated places, existing licenses, leases, management agreements, and inclusive of any additional land).    
* Refundable Accommodation Deposit (RAD) liability (value net of RAD liability).    
Retirement Village / Land Lease Communities (with DMFs)
*Existing Property - Owners’ Interest (subject to existing resident agreements and inclusive of any additional land).    
To be Developed
*Market Value "As Is" (assuming the planning permit is in place and registration of subdivision/amalgamation of the site has been completed).    
*Project Related Site Value / Residual Value (subject to the proposed development scheme).    
*Gross Realisation of "As If Complete" proposed Independent Living Apartments (assuming all proposed apartments are satisfactorily completed).    
*Current Hypothetical Market Value of proposed Deferred Management Fee (DMF) "As If Complete" (for the completed Village).    
Hospitals/Day Surgeries/Medical Centres
*Existing Property - Market Value (on a "Going Concern" basis, exclusive of GST, subject to existing licenses, leases, management agreements, and inclusive of any additional land). 
*Market Value (on an "In Use" basis, exclusive of GST).    
*"Alternative Use - with vacant possession" basis assessment.    
To be Developed
*Market Value "As Is" (exclusive of GST, subject to the development approval).    
*Project Related Site Value / Residual Value (subject to the proposed development scheme).    
*Market Value "As If Complete" (on a "Going Concern" basis, exclusive of GST, subject to existing licenses, leases, management agreements, and inclusive of any additional land).    
*Market Value "As If Complete" (on an "In Use" basis, exclusive of GST).    
*"Alternative Use - with vacant possession" basis assessment.

sections.Additional requirement:
General notes
*Market values should not include stock on hand.    
*Market Value "In Use" adheres to the Market Value definition, with the added condition that the enterprise will continue operating for the foreseeable future. It does not include Goodwill or any brand value. The Alternative Use Assessment reflects open market value subject to vacant possession.    
*For Specialised Properties, a Project Related Site Value is only required when a hypothetical development/feasibility analysis is appropriate.

sections.Replacement Insurance Assessment:
A value exclusive of GST for insurance purposes inclusive of removal of debris, professional fees and replacement costs, cost escalation for design, planning and construction. A calculation of loss of rent/income/outgoings is not required.

- Where the valuer is unable to provide a replacement insurance assessment, a recommendation for a QS verified estimate (in lieu of valuer estimate) should include supporting justification.
sections.Executive Summary:
*Where the primary basis of valuation is to be a Freehold Going Concern, regulatory requirements also necessitate provision of a Freehold Lessor’s Interest Value (net of letting up allowance to attract a lessee) to ascertain the underlying real estate only value.
*When there is an absence of sufficient market evidence to support the Freehold Lessor’s Interest Value (net of letting up allowance to attract a lessee), the valuer is to use expert judgement and industry benchmarks to assess a notional rental and capitalisation rate in order to calculate a hypothetical value. The report may include an explanatory comment to that effect
*The further apportionment of Freehold Going Concern values into notional component values is not required, although summating components may be used as a check method.

sections.Valuation Assessment:
Existing Property:
*Market Value subject to SDA cashflow (exclusive of GST).
*Alternative Use Value assuming disposal “In One Line” (Net of remediation costs to achieve alternative use).
To be Developed:
*Market Value “As Is” exclusive of GST, subject to the development approval issued by the relevant Authority;
*Project Related Site Value / Residual Value subject to the proposed development
scheme;
*Market Value “As if Complete” subject to SDA cashflow (exclusive of GST).
*“As if Complete” Alternative Use value assuming disposal “In One Line” (Net of
remediation costs to achieve alternative use).
Market Value subject to SDA cashflow encompasses the various ownership / management structures including:
*Freehold Owner leases the property to an SDA Provider;
*Freehold Owner employs an SDA Provider to manage the SDA affairs, with income to the Freehold Owner based on a share of the SDA income;
*Freehold Owner is also the approved SDA Provider (under separate companies) and receives 100% of the SDA income in which case Valuers are to deduct an SDA management fee from the SDA income. 

*For Specialised Properties, a Project Related Site Value is only required when using a hypothetical development/feasibility analysis valuation methodology.    
*Existing Properties: Report the lower of: Market Value subject to SDA cash flow.    
*Alternative Use Value, assuming disposal "In One Line" (net of remediation costs to achieve alternative use).    
*To be Developed Properties: Report the lower of:Market Value "As Is".    
*Project Related Site Value / Residual Value.

sections.Economic Commentary:
The Bank requires both a current and forward-looking view (typically 3-5 years) rather than just an historic view of market conditions. 
- Brief overview of the macro market and economic conditions relevant to the property.
sections.Market Commentary:
The market commentary should be specific to the property being valued. Generic or irrelevant market commentary should be avoided. Typically, this commentary on market conditions specific to the property should include:
- Investment activity including depth of the market, current sentiment, yield/capital value/land value trends and identification of key ‘players’.
- Leasing activity including vacancy rates, incentives, rental level trends and likely additions to supply.
- A discussion of the major drivers of supply / user demand over the period under review. A detailed analysis of current and potential supply may be required in certain instances (as appropriate). 

Shopping Centre
• Comment on the property’s trade catchment area(s) with emphasis on likely changes to population growth patterns,
demographics, household income, unemployment, geographic boundaries of catchment.
• Comment on competition within the trade catchment area(s), centre’s growth prospects, proposed new competition and the
current performance of other major competitors/potential extensions to centres.
• The group of shopping centres utilised for rental comparison purposes should be clearly listed.
sections.Marketing Period:
*Provide an opinion of the likely buyer profile / type and estimated selling period. If the selling period is greater than 6 months,
then provide an explanation for this selling period.
• If partial interests, advise if co-owners agreement(s) have been reviewed and detail any onerous terms, saleability and liquidity
concerns and marketing period to realise the partial interest assessment.
sections.Sales/Pre-Sales/Leases:
• Specifics of the last sale of the property (if within the last five years) should be included within the Valuation. More specifically, date of sale, consideration, and any other relevant details
• Details relating to a recent or active sale of the property should also be stated. A full contract of sale should be sighted. The Valuation should reconcile the value assessed with the sale price and if any variances if exceeding or below value, these should be commented upon with reasoning fully explaining the difference. Advise if the property was formally marketed for sale
• If the property or part of the property is currently available for sale or lease, comments as to the current saleability / lettability should be included along with how long on the market and if the property is being professional marketed. 
• Detail if the property is managed competently and appropriately for the type of property by an experienced property manager.
sections.Sales Evidence:
*Follow Valuation Standards: Adhere to IVS, API, and/or RICS guidance on comparable evidence selection and analysis
*Clear Presentation:  Provide a summary of sales and leasing comparables, preferably in table format, with full analysis of each transaction.
*Consistent Analysis: Ensure the level of analysis is consistent with the valuation methodology and broken down into appropriate units of comparison.  Note any unavailable information as "unknown."
*Comparable Identification: Include sufficient details (including addresses) for each comparable to allow for easy identification.
*Relativity Analysis: Comment on the relativity of each comparable to the subject property, explaining how it was used to form the market value opinion.
*Relevant Comparables Only: Utilise only appropriate sales and leasing comparables that directly relate to the valuation approach.
*Unsettled Sales:  If relying on unsettled/agent-advised sales, comment on whether contract details were sighted and, if not, disclose the source of the sales information.
*For Sale/On Market Evidence: Present "for sale" or "on market" evidence as separate commentary, not within the transacted comparable evidence section.
sections.Rental Evidence:
As per above - plus 
* A summary of the rental comparables considered in determining the market rental for all components of the property should be included. A summary of each comparable rental is required, including address/unit no, brief description of key characteristics,
lettable area, commencement date, term, rental (analysed in same manner as the adopted approach for the market rents for the subject), outgoings, incentives/rebates, reviews, tenant details/name (where available). The relatively of each comparable to the subject is required i.e. inferior / superior / similar. 
A valuation that doesn’t include adequate comparability comments may be returned for amendment.
sections.Valuation Methodology:
Income Analysis:
*Provide a detailed and self-explanatory cash flow analysis.
*Show detailed calculations for rent reversions.
*Itemise all outgoings in a schedule, comparing to actuals and commenting on variances.
*Analyse letting prospects for vacant space and expiring leases.

Shopping Centre
• Comment on trading history of centre and show calculations for percentage rents (if applicable).
• Comment on trading performance (including by trade category and tenant type) and mix of tenants relative to similar centres and / or industry averages / previous year performance.
• Provide percentage rent projections (where applicable) for major tenancies.

* Indicate the basis upon which the Valuation has been assessed. Selection of the method of Valuation is the responsibility of the Valuer, however typically it would be envisaged that at least two methods would need to be adopted.
*All assumptions must be explained and justified. Should the Valuation inadequately address all assumptions /inputs it will be returned for amendment.
• All Valuation calculations are to be included or annexed to the valuation. ‘Retention of calculations on file’ not shown in the Valuation is unacceptable.
• Should you determine that the highest and best use of a leased or investment property is for redevelopment (also refer to other relevant chapters of these Valuation Standards), the Bank may also require an assessment on a ‘continued use’ or ‘alternative use’ basis. This should be discussed / agreed with the Bank to determine if an additional assessment is required prior to
finalisation of the valuation.
sections.Valuation Assessment:
• Fully disclose all Valuation calculations (i.e. actual and / or estimated rentals, itemised property expenses, capitalisation rate, rent reversions and letting up / rent incentives) resulting in the assessed value.
• As a general guide (dependant on asset type), a full analysis of individual comparable sales should include, but not be limited to, address, sale date, sale price, brief description, passing and market rental assessment, WALE, passing initial yield, market or equivalent yield, rate psm of building area, rate psm of land area improved. When adopting the DCF approach, comparable evidence analysis should include IRR, growth rates adopted, capital expenditure, speculative renewal assumptions, terminal yield etc.
• A sensitivity analysis of the value based on the major variables is required.
• Rental Reversion Calculations (passing versus market) on a tenant by tenant basis should be clearly shown in workings.
• Capital Adjustments adopted within the Capitalisation Approach must be fully outlined/explained allowing the reader to be able to easily calculate and interpret all adjustments. The level and types of capital adjustment adopt should align with the analysis of sales evidence or otherwise appropriate commentary provided for any variance
sections.GST:
* Ensure your Valuation calculations account for GST and addresses the GST status of the property. All assessed values are to be expressed inclusive and exclusive o  GST, where appropriate. Please advise the Bank immediately if you are unsure of the appropriate treatment for GST. 
*The Bank seeks a common sense approach to GST and valuers are not expected to be tax experts, however, should be based upon the most reasonable knowledge of the latest GST legislation
*In respect of Development Valuations, ensure your cashflow and project feasibility express all development costs inclusive of GST. A separate budget category for input tax credits should be included in the cashflow. The cashflow is to assume all tax credits are received from the ATO two months after the input tax was incurred.
*The General Tax Rule should be utilised unless documentary evidence has been provided to justify use of the Margin Scheme Rule. If the GST exclusive figure has been determined by use of the Margin Scheme, then documentary evidence justifying its use together with appropriate commentary to the calculations should be included within the Valuation annexures and / or report.
sections.Additional requirement:
ESG:
*‘assess the extent to which the subject property currently meets the sustainability and ESG criteria typically expected within the context of its market standing and arrive at an informed view on the likelihood of these impacting on value, e.g. how a well-informed purchaser would take account of them in making a decision as to offer price
*provide a description of the sustainability-related property characteristics and attributes that have been collected
*provide a statement of their opinion on the relationship between sustainability factors and the resultant valuation, including a comment on the current benefits/risks that are associated with these sustainability characteristics, or the lack of risks and
* provide an opinion on the potential impact of these benefits and/or risks to relative property values over time.’
Additionally: 
*When ESG factors impact value, valuers must gather relevant ESG data from various sources (customer, third parties, public resources).
*This data should be summarised within the valuation or qualified if unavailable.
*Clearly explain how ESG characteristics affect the valuation approach and calculations.
*Detail how the subject property's ESG characteristics compare to the expected ESG criteria within its market/competitor set.
*Address any identified risk of material obsolescence due to upcoming regulations (e.g., minimum energy efficiency standards).
*If the owner indicates a compliance pathway, detail the approach and costs involved.
sections.Replacement Insurance Assessment:
A Valuation must provide a building insurance assessment (both exclusive and inclusive of GST). The Valuation should show all calculations / workings incorporating the following:
- Costs for demolition, removal of debris and clearing site for reconstruction.
- All professional fees.
- All reconstruction costs including any council and statutory authority fees.
- Inflation allowance on all costs through the insurance period from the date of Valuation.
- Inflation through approvals, reconstruction, and re-leasing period.
- Loss of rent / re-leasing costs.
- An adequate contingency factor
In instances that a building insurance assessment cannot be completed and requires additional expert advice (i.e. heritage or highly specialised property), you should initial contact the Bank for instructions prior to finalisation of the Valuation. Furthermore, the Valuation should also alert the Bank to engaging additional expert services.

sections.Valuation Methodology:
• Indicate the basis upon which the Valuation has been assessed. As noted above, appropriate selection of the method of Valuation is the responsibility of the Valuer. However typically it would be envisaged that at least two methods would need to be adopted; one of which would be a residual method both on a discounted cashflow basis and a traditional hypothetical development basis (where appropriate).
• Fully disclose all Valuation calculations including any discounted cash flow, input, or summary sheets. A copy of the computer file workings may be requested. If utilising ‘Estate Master’, include all workings such as Cashflow, Input and Summary sheets etc.
• All project outlays and revenues should be clearly identified with appropriate allowances for likely lead times required to achieve development approvals and / or rezoning and any infrastructure works required to undertake the project.
• The required discount rate (IRR) or profit and risk margin used to establish the residual value must be fully explained and supported by market-based analysis/comparable evidence.
• A sensitivity analysis should be undertaken having regard to the following variables:
  - Rate of sale.
  - Profit Margin / IRR
  - Interest rate.
  - Gross Realisation.
  - Development costs; and
  - Development timing.
sections.Valuation Assessment:
Market Value "As Is": Reported both net and gross of GST.
-For site finance/assessment: Use residual/feasibility analysis and direct comparison, reflecting market participant approaches.
-For site finance (not construction funding): May require "continued use" or "alternative use" assessment, especially for sites without development approvals.

Gross Realisation "As If Complete": Reported both net and gross of GST.
-Reflect current market conditions, not forecasted values.
-Provide individual values within the valuation.

Market Value "As If Complete" (In One Line): May be required, considering factors like market rentals, vacancy, outgoings, and lease-up rates.

Construction Funding Valuation - Only undertake when:
-All planning approvals are in place.
-Construction costs, statutory costs, and timeframe are known and verified.
-Presales are executed and legally enforceable.
-Confirm transferability of intellectual property and materials.

Residual Analysis: If different from Market Value, explain reasons for discrepancies.
-Exclude escalation/inflation.
-Assume 100% borrowings.
-Report Profit and Risk Margin/IRR after interest.
sections.GST:
* Ensure your Valuation calculations account for GST and addresses the GST status of the property. All assessed values are to be expressed inclusive and exclusive o  GST, where appropriate. Please advise the Bank immediately if you are unsure of the appropriate treatment for GST. 
*The Bank seeks a common sense approach to GST and valuers are not expected to be tax experts, however, should be based upon the most reasonable knowledge of the latest GST legislation
*In respect of Development Valuations, ensure your cashflow and project feasibility express all development costs inclusive of GST. A separate budget category for input tax credits should be included in the cashflow. The cashflow is to assume all tax credits are received from the ATO two months after the input tax was incurred.
*The General Tax Rule should be utilised unless documentary evidence has been provided to justify use of the Margin Scheme Rule. If the GST exclusive figure has been determined by use of the Margin Scheme, then documentary evidence justifying its use together with appropriate commentary to the calculations should be included within the Valuation annexures and / or report.

*If the owner indicates a compliance pathway, detail the approach and costs involved.
sections.Replacement Insurance Assessment:
A Valuation must provide a building insurance assessment (both exclusive and inclusive of GST). The Valuation should show all calculations / workings incorporating the following:
- Costs for demolition, removal of debris and clearing site for reconstruction.
- All professional fees.
- All reconstruction costs including any council and statutory authority fees.
- Inflation allowance on all costs through the insurance period from the date of Valuation.
- Inflation through approvals, reconstruction, and re-leasing period.
- Loss of rent / re-leasing costs.
- An adequate contingency factor
In instances that a building insurance assessment cannot be completed and requires additional expert advice (i.e. heritage or highly specialised property), you should initial contact the Bank for instructions prior to finalisation of the Valuation. Furthermore, the Valuation should also alert the Bank to engaging additional expert services.

sections.Valuation Methodology:
• Indicate the basis upon which the Valuation has been assessed. Selection of the method of Valuation is the responsibility of the Valuer having regard to the type of development. However typically it would be envisaged that at least two methods would need to be adopted.
• Fully disclose all residual calculations including any discounted cash flow, input, or summary sheets. A copy of the computer file workings may be requested. Fully disclose all ‘As If Complete’ calculations. If utilising ‘Estate Master’, include all workings such as Cashflow, Input and Summary sheets etc.
• All project outlays and revenues should be clearly identified with appropriate allowances for likely lead times required to achieve development approvals and / or rezoning and any upfront infrastructure works required to undertake the project.
• Analysis is to be undertaken on the sensitivity of any indicated values having regard to changes in:

sections.Valuation Assessment:
Construction Funding Valuation - Only undertake when:

-Construction costs, statutory costs, and timeframe are known and verified.
-Presales/preleases are executed and legally enforceable.
-Confirm transferability of intellectual property and materials

Residual Analysis:
-If different from Market Value, explain reasons for discrepancies.

-Assume 100% borrowings.
-Report Profit and Risk Margin/IRR after interest.

Commercial, Retail, or Industrial Developments:
-Market Value "As If Complete": Based on actual/anticipated preleasing/presale commitments.
-Gross Realisation "As If Complete": If the project will be subdivided or sold in components.--
-Market Value "As If Complete" (Vacant Possession)

Accommodation/Hotel Developments:
-Market Value "As If Complete" (Going Concern, Day One Trading)
-Market Value "As If Complete" (Going Concern, Fully Traded Up)
sections.GST:
* Ensure your Valuation calculations account for GST and addresses the GST status of the property. All assessed values are to be expressed inclusive and exclusive o  GST, where appropriate. Please advise the Bank immediately if you are unsure of the appropriate treatment for GST. 
*The Bank seeks a common sense approach to GST and valuers are not expected to be tax experts, however, should be based upon the most reasonable knowledge of the latest GST legislation
*In respect of Development Valuations, ensure your cashflow and project feasibility express all development costs inclusive of GST. A separate budget category for input tax credits should be included in the cashflow. The cashflow is to assume all tax credits are received from the ATO two months after the input tax was incurred.
*The General Tax Rule should be utilised unless documentary evidence has been provided to justify use of the Margin Scheme Rule. If the GST exclusive figure has been determined by use of the Margin Scheme, then documentary evidence justifying its use together with appropriate commentary to the calculations should be included within the Valuation annexures and / or report.
sections.Additional requirement:
ESG:
*‘assess the extent to which the subject property currently meets the sustainability and ESG criteria typically expected within the context of its market standing and arrive at an informed view on the likelihood of these impacting on value, e.g. how a well-informed purchaser would take account of them in making a decision as to offer price
*provide a description of the sustainability-related property characteristics and attributes that have been collected
*provide a statement of their opinion on the relationship between sustainability factors and the resultant valuation, including a comment on the current benefits/risks that are associated with these sustainability characteristics, or the lack of risks and
* provide an opinion on the potential impact of these benefits and/or risks to relative property values over time.’
Additionally: 
*When ESG factors impact value, valuers must gather relevant ESG data from various sources (customer, third parties, public resources).
*This data should be summarised within the valuation or qualified if unavailable.
*Clearly explain how ESG characteristics affect the valuation approach and calculations.
*Detail how the subject property's ESG characteristics compare to the expected ESG criteria within its market/competitor set.
*Address any identified risk of material obsolescence due to upcoming regulations (e.g., minimum energy efficiency standards).
*If the owner indicates a compliance pathway, detail the approach and costs involved.
sections.Replacement Insurance Assessment:
A Valuation must provide a building insurance assessment (both exclusive and inclusive of GST). The Valuation should show all calculations / workings incorporating the following:
- Costs for demolition, removal of debris and clearing site for reconstruction.
- All professional fees.
- All reconstruction costs including any council and statutory authority fees.
- Inflation allowance on all costs through the insurance period from the date of Valuation.
- Inflation through approvals, reconstruction, and re-leasing period.
- Loss of rent / re-leasing costs.
- An adequate contingency factor
In instances that a building insurance assessment cannot be completed and requires additional expert advice (i.e. heritage or highly specialised property), you should initial contact the Bank for instructions prior to finalisation of the Valuation. Furthermore, the Valuation should also alert the Bank to engaging additional expert services.

sections.Environmental:
*Valuers must identify and alert the bank to any potential environmental risks.
*Site inspections, including checks of surrounding areas, are mandatory.
*Recommendations for further assessment by qualified professionals should be made if necessary.

sections.Market Commentary:

- Building activity including competition and likely additions to supply. A detailed commentary on the current and potential competition is required including specifics on individual projects. A Valuer should consider a model of future supply and demand to project average occupancies and room rates within the market and to form the basis of a fair market share assessment.
- A discussion of the major drivers of supply / user demand over the period under review.
-Analysis the current state of the hotel and tourism industry and detail any changes (current or anticipated) which may impact on the long-term viability of the property.

sections.GST:
* Ensure your Valuation calculations account for GST and addresses the GST status of the property. All assessed values are to be expressed inclusive and exclusive o  GST, where appropriate. Please advise the Bank immediately if you are unsure of the appropriate treatment for GST.

*In respect of Development Valuations, ensure your cashflow and project feasibility express all development costs inclusive of GST. sections.Replacement Insurance Assessment:
A Valuation must provide a building insurance assessment (both exclusive and inclusive of GST). The Valuation should show all calculations / workings incorporating the following:
- Costs for demolition, removal of debris and clearing site for reconstruction.
- All professional fees.
- All reconstruction costs including any council and statutory authority fees.
- Inflation allowance on all costs through the insurance period from the date of Valuation.
- Inflation through approvals, reconstruction, and re-leasing period.
- Loss of rent / re-leasing costs.
- An adequate contingency factor
In instances that a building insurance assessment cannot be completed and requires additional expert advice (i.e. heritage or highly specialised property), you should initial contact the Bank for instructions prior to finalisation of the Valuation. Furthermore, the Valuation should also alert the Bank to engaging additional expert services.

sections.Tenancy/Income Details:
Document Review:
-Review all relevant tenancy documents (leases, licenses, agreements).
-Clearly state if leases were not sighted.
-Review all major leases and a representative sample of non-major leases.
-Highlight any onerous clauses (acknowledge valuer is not a legal expert).
Lease Completeness:
-Ensure leases are fully executed and complete.
-Delay valuation if necessary.
Tenancy Schedule: Provide a tenancy schedule for multi-tenanted properties, summarizing key lease details.
Lease Terms & Rent:
-Consider impact of rent reviews, remaining lease terms, and option periods.
-Confirm actual rent received and comment on market rent levels.
-Address potential vacancies, re-lettability, letting-up allowances, and tenant outgoings.
Arrears & Disputes:
-Obtain a schedule of rental and outgoings arrears (if applicable).
-Include details of tenancy disputes.
Weighted Average Lease Expiry (WALE):
- Calculate WALE by income and area, including vacant space, owner-occupied areas, and monthly tenancies at market rent (for a term of 1 day).
- Do not assume a notional commercial lease term.
Tenant Retention: Provide an opinion on the likely tenant retention rate.
Proposed Developments: Comment on the achievability of rental levels, letting-up periods, incentives, and market competition for proposed developments.
Owner-Occupied Premises: Disclose assumed notional lease terms, conditions, review mechanisms, and incentives.
Valuation Considerations: Consider the existing tenancy position in the valuation.
Tenant/Co-owner Rights: Highlight any tenant/co-owner purchase rights and their impact on saleability/value.

sections.Valuation Methodology:
• The valuation rationale is to be supported by at least one check method. Reasons should be provided as to why a particular approach is deemed to be most reliable.

 • For tenanted properties, a discounted cash flow for a period of five to ten years is to be provided, where appropriate or when requested. sections.Valuation Methodology:
• Undertake residual analysis / feasibility over the life of the project, if less than three years. The valuation is to assume 100% borrowings with any Internal Rate of Return or Profit and Risk analysis to be presented on an after interest basis. Except where easily verified, ANZ does not take into account inflated costs or realisations. 

• Any analysis should be on present day values and conditions. For projects running longer than three years, the longer term en-globo land value is to be assessed on a per hectare, broadacre basis, although (where possible) a residual analysis / feasibility should be undertaken as a check method.

• The cash flow analysis (where required, including where the development period including selling period is less than 36 months) for initial stages must include an explanation and concise summary of the critical assumptions utilised. Inflows, outflows, net cash flow, interest, soft costs including separating marketing costs from and selling costs, development margin and internal rates of return are required to be separately itemised (a copy of the computer file may be required).

• Comment on whether the development reaches acceptable profitability benchmarks (i.e. development
margin, IRR before and after interest). Where developments fall outside acceptable parameters, please
provide a more detailed rationale as to the reason for the differences. A builder’s margin and contingency allowance are to be included in all feasibilities.

• Undertake a sensitivity analysis showing the impact on value of variations in sales rates, gross realisations and development costs.
sections.Valuation Assessment:
• An “As If Complete” value of the proposed project as at the date of valuation on a GST inclusive and exclusive basis (where applicable).
• Land Value “As Is”, i.e. reflective of the current zoning and planning approvals in place but with no other assumptions.
• A residual feasibility analysis of the project should be undertaken in addition to the above Land Value “As Is” assessment. This may require the reporting of a residual value or “Project Related Site Value” for construction funding purposes as instructed and / or depending on the current development status / nature.
• ANZ requires the feasibility to contemplate initial stages not exceeding a development period including selling period of 36 months, with the balance of the land treated as en-globo (in land subdivisions for example);

• An “As Is” value of stock on hand (if any). An “In One Line” assessment may also be necessary if it is considered that the stock will take longer than 9-12 months to sell and settle, or if specifically requested by PR-TS.
• Residual en-globo land assessment upon completion (of construction) of the current proposed stage(s).
sections.GST: • GST needs to appropriately identified and treated. AE.notes: •The valuation of these assets may only be completed by a Panel Valuer who specialises in this sector and is appointed as a Panel Valuer. •Each facility is to be valued on a stand-alone basis with any economies of scale or other benefits associated with more than one facility to be ignored. • In all cases, all assumptions and calculations must be provided with a high degree of transparency so that the reader can clearly understand how the value was derived. • The “going concern” business assessment (“Core Value” or “Net Value”) is to disregard RAD’s, Accommodation Bonds other than periodic payments / DAP income and Retention amounts. This method specifically excludes notional credit interest earnings from these bonds if invested. Likewise, assets that include other income sources such as but not limited to Community Care, home care, supported residential services or respite service should have these components assessed separately. • Where an asset is subject to a third party, arm’s length lease this needs to be closely examined as to sustainability of net passing income with reference to known market parameters.
